literal: By wealth is possible everything, thinking thus, without giving, he who hoards, by that delusion, arises an ignoble birth.
translation: For the miser who hoards without giving, thinking that everything can be achieved through wealth, an ignoble birth will arise from that very delusion.
modern: செல்வத்தினால் எல்லாம் முடியும் என்று எண்ணி, பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்காமல் சேர்த்து வைக்கும் பேராசைக்காரனுக்கு, அந்த அறியாமையினால் பெருமையற்ற பிறவி உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the delusion of hoarding wealth without sharing it. The miser falsely believes that money alone can secure everything in life, leading them to withhold charity. This mental blindness or delusion (maruḷ) is what ultimately causes them to be reborn into an ignoble, unworthy state (māṇāp piṟappu). The poet highlights that wealth is useless if not given to those in need, and the obsession with hoarding only degrades one's character and future.
